payload.name: Preserve explicit source or discovery detail with event memories
payload.description: When extracting or updating a memory of an event and the speaker also states how they learned about or discovered it (e.g., saw a flyer, heard from a friend, read online), include that source/discovery detail in the memory content.
content: During extraction, if a statement contains both an event and the explicit way the person learned about, found, or discovered that event, preserve the source/discovery detail in the same memory or as a separate linked memory; do not record only the event outcome.
When updating an existing event memory, carry forward any explicit source/discovery detail from the original or new evidence, adding it to the memory content instead of dropping it.

solves: The diagnosed cause is that extraction recorded an event (signing up for a workshop) but omitted the explicitly stated discovery mechanism (saw a flyer). The abstract failure is losing the 'how the person learned about it' detail when an event and its source are mentioned together. The proposed rule preserves explicit source/discovery details in memory, making later 'how did X hear about Y' questions answerable. It applies to any future extraction or update where a speaker states how they learned about, found, or discovered an event.
